messages:
jen: Heads-up: just started a staged rollout of 'latency-squeeze-v1' across production GPU pools. Short wins in canary: p50 ~11% lower, p99 ~22% lower, and token cost ~8% lower for conversational workloads. Rolling with gentle ramps. :rocket:

deploy-bot: canary summary (canary-7 -> prod):
- p50: 92ms -> 82ms (-10.9%)
- p99: 460ms -> 359ms (-22%)
- token unit $: $0.0091 -> $0.0084 (-7.7%)
- request errors: 0.015% -> 0.02% (no alerts)

avi: solid. what's in the change? scheduler tweaks or cache?

jen: combo of changes: 1) microbatcher now uses a predictive hold of up to 7ms on tiny requests if a matching prefix is expected (model-agnostic hinting), 2) lightweight shadow LRU for hot prefix prefetch to cut remote fetches on tail requests, 3) slight timebox adjustment to preserve p99. No model weights altered.

karim: rollback/kill switch? want to hook this into our incident runbooks.

jen: yes 99feature flag `runtime.latency_squeeze_v1` per-pool. Rollback endpoint: `POST /release/flags/runtime.latency_squeeze_v1/disable` with body `{"pool":"<pool>"}`. Added to runbook: https://go/redwood/runbooks/latency-squeeze-v1

ops-bot: note: Dedicated customers will receive it enabled by default. To opt out, set `runtime.disable_latency_optimizations=true` in tenant config. Logged compatibility notes for >64k token jobs.

nora: can we get the quick canary check command to validate pools?

karim: dropping the check we used:
```
# compare p99 per pool between canary and prod
python infra/compare_metrics.py --metric p99_latency --from canary-7 --to prod --group pool
```

avi: please put a 1-line for ops channel and for customer-success with the opt-out link.

jen: on it. Draft blurb: "Launched latency-squeeze-v1: p50 ~-11%, p99 ~-22%, token cost ~-8%. Opt-out via runtime.disable_latency_optimizations. See runbook." :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: feature `runtime.latency_squeeze_v1` enabled on: gpu-us-west-2a, gpu-eu-west-1b. Canary -> full in 22m.

jen: thanks all 99huge thanks to the microbatch + prefetch teams. I'll follow up with a short post including a couple of latency and cost graphs later today. :party_parrot:
